implementation_notes: Scala's premature optimisation has a few characteristic forms. `Array[Int]` over `List[Int]` is the right call for a measured hot path and pure style otherwise, and getting it wrong for the wrong reason costs readability. Boxing collections to avoid primitive-specialised variants is a JVM-specific trap. `import scala.annotation.tailrec` is often added because the compiler warning appeared, when the real fix is to restructure the loop — and a genuine tail call on a large structure can overflow anyway. On the JVM, the allocation profile is the measurement that matters, and it is cheap to take.
idiom_name: boxing to avoid primitive arrays; tail-recursion annotation as a speed fix
pitfalls: `Array` used everywhere for speed, which loses slicing and the collection API for no measured gain.
Guava/Scala boxed collections to dodge primitive specialisation, which often allocates more, not less.
`@tailrec` added to silence a warning while the real cost is an unnecessary recursive structure.
Micro-optimising the JVM warmup path — profile after the JIT has settled, not on the first thousand iterations.
